name: Record an approved fee reduction, by discretionary concession or by scholarship won on a test
priorityReason: Every invoice run reads the concession. Without it a family entitled to a reduction is billed the full amount.

goal.capability: to record that a student pays a reduced fee, and why
goal.outcome: the reduction reaches every invoice by itself, and the reason it was granted can be answered years later

preconditions.condition: The student is enrolled and belongs to a class with an approved fee structure.
An authenticated session exists. Recording requires Accounts; approving requires School Admin, or the Principal for a scholarship.

A chart of accounts exists, so the reduction can be reported against fee income.

postConditions: An approved reduction is stored against the student with its validity period, and every subsequent invoice applies it automatically.
The written reason is on the record, so why a family pays less can be answered years afterwards.
A scholarship award carries the test and the score it was won on, so a discretionary favour and an earned award are not confused.
The reduction has an end date and is surfaced for review when it is reached, so a concession granted for one hard year does not run for five.
Invoices already issued are untouched. A reduction applies from its effective date onward.
The reduction is visible on the invoice as its own line, so a family can see what they were granted.
Nothing was reduced without approval. A reduction recorded by Accounts alone bills nobody.

dataFields.name: Type
dataFields.validation: What kind of reduction this is. It decides who approves it (BR-3).

dataFields.name: Percentage
dataFields.validation: Greater than zero and not more than 100.

dataFields.name: Fixed amount
dataFields.validation: Greater than zero, and not more than the fee it reduces (BR-6).

dataFields.name: Applies to
dataFields.validation: Which fee types the reduction covers. A transport concession must not reduce tuition (BR-5).

dataFields.validation: 20 to 1000 characters. Mandatory. A reduction cannot be recorded without a written statement of why (BR-2).
dataFields.example: Father's business closed in March; two siblings enrolled; verified by home visit on 12-04-2026.

dataFields.name: Supporting document
dataFields.validation: Evidence supporting the request, held against the record.

dataFields.name: Valid to
dataFields.validation: Mandatory. A reduction with no end date runs forever and is never reviewed (BR-9).

dataFields.name: Test
dataFields.validation: The scholarship test the award was won on.

dataFields.name: Score
dataFields.validation: The candidate's score, carried from the test rather than typed (BR-4).

dataFields.validation: Maximum 500 characters. Required when returning a reduction unapproved.
dataFields.example: No supporting evidence attached — attach the income statement.

businessRules.rule: A reduction is recorded by one person and approved by another. A reduction recorded by Accounts alone bills nobody, because reducing what a family pays is not a clerical act.
A written reason is mandatory. A reduction cannot be recorded without a statement of why, since a family paying less than their neighbour is a question the school must be able to answer.

A concession or a discount is approved by the School Admin. A scholarship is approved by the Principal, because it is awarded on merit and is a claim about the school's standards as much as its finances.
A scholarship carries the test and the score it was won on, taken from the marked result rather than typed. Otherwise a discretionary favour and an earned award become indistinguishable.
A reduction names which fee types it covers. A transport concession must not silently reduce tuition.
A reduction may not exceed the fee it reduces. There is no route by which a concession pays a family.
Every approved reduction is applied automatically to every subsequent invoice. Nobody remembers to apply it, and nobody can forget.
A reduction applies from its effective date onward and never recalculates an invoice already issued.
Every reduction has an end date and is surfaced for review when it is reached. A concession granted for one hard year must not still be running five years later because nobody looked.
A reduction is withdrawn rather than deleted, and the withdrawal carries its own reason. The record of what a family was granted survives.

A student may hold more than one reduction — a sibling discount and a transport concession — provided they apply to different fee types. Two reductions on the same fee type are not stacked without an explicit decision.
The reason recorded is not shown to the family. It may concern their circumstances, and a parent reading the school's assessment of their finances helps nobody.

transitions.condition: Approved by the role the type requires (BR-3).

basicFlow.navigation: Login → Fee → Concessions and scholarships → Record concession
basicFlow.userAction: Selects the student and enters the reduction as a percentage or a fixed amount, naming the fee types it covers.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Checks the value is above zero and does not exceed the fee it reduces.

basicFlow.userAction: Writes the reason and sets the validity period.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Requires a written reason and an end date, and refuses without either.
Routes it to the School Admin, or to the Principal where the type is a scholarship.

basicFlow.navigation: Login → Fee → Concessions and scholarships → Approve
basicFlow.userAction: Reviews the reduction and its reason and approves it.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Records the approval and stores the reduction against the student with its validity period.
Applies the reduction automatically to every subsequent invoice from its effective date, leaving issued invoices untouched.
Surfaces the reduction for review when its validity period ends, and stops applying it.

basicFlow.userAction: Renews the reduction for a further period, or lets it lapse.
basicFlow.systemResponse: A renewal goes through approval again rather than extending silently.

alternateFlows.condition: The reduction is a scholarship rather than a concession
alternateFlows.navigation: Login → Examination → Scholarship test → Mark → Fee → Scholarship award
alternateFlows.behaviour: A test is created, candidates sit it, and those who perform are put forward with their scores. The award carries the test and the score, so an earned award is distinguishable from a discretionary favour (BR-4).
The Principal approves it, not the School Admin, because a scholarship is a claim about the school's standards as much as its finances (BR-3).

alternateFlows.condition: The approver does not accept the reduction
alternateFlows.navigation: Concessions and scholarships → Return with a reason
alternateFlows.behaviour: It returns to Accounts with a written reason and nothing is reduced in the meantime.

alternateFlows.condition: The student already holds a reduction on another fee type
alternateFlows.behaviour: Both may be held provided they cover different fee types. Two reductions on the same fee type are not stacked without an explicit decision (BR-11).

alternateFlows.condition: Circumstances change before the validity period ends
alternateFlows.behaviour: The reduction is withdrawn early with its own reason. It is not deleted, so the record of what was granted survives (BR-10).
A renewal is proposed for a further period and goes through approval again, rather than the original running on unexamined (BR-9).

departures.requirement: An approved reduction is applied by the invoice run itself. There is no screen on which somebody applies a concession to a bill, because that is where they get forgotten.
A reduction stops applying on its end date without anybody intervening, and is surfaced for review at that point.

openQuestions.question: May two reductions be stacked on the same fee type, and who decides?
openQuestions.assumption: Not without an explicit decision (BR-11). The mechanism for that decision is not specified.

openQuestions.question: Is there a value or percentage above which the Principal rather than the School Admin should approve a concession?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified. A full fee waiver is a governance matter.

openQuestions.question: Does a scholarship carry through to the next academic session automatically, or is it re-awarded each year?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified, and families will assume it continues.

openQuestions.question: What proportion of students may hold a reduction before the school's budget is affected, and does anybody watch that?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified. The report shows value forgone but nothing enforces a ceiling.

openQuestions.question: Should the family be told the reason recorded, or only the value?
openQuestions.assumption: Only the value (BR-12). Confirm the school agrees.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: academic-session-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every academic record carries an academic session ID. Lists default to the current open session.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: money
conventionsApplied.rule: All monetary values are stored as fixed-point decimals in the smallest currency unit, never as floating point. Displayed as PKR with a thousands separator and two decimal places. Rounding is half-up at the line.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: attachments
conventionsApplied.rule: Uploaded files are limited to 10 MB and to PDF, JPG, PNG, DOCX and XLSX unless a use case states otherwise. File type is validated by content, not by extension.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
